html:
The Nisenan are a people of California's Sacramento Valley and the Sierra Nevada foothills, along the Yuba, Bear and American rivers. They are often classed as the southern branch of the Maidu, though some Nisenan dispute the link. See Mountain Maidu.

They lived in villages of up to a few hundred people, ate acorns as their staple, fished for salmon and traded with the Miwok and Patwin. An epidemic, probably malaria, killed many in 1833. Then in January 1848 gold was found at Sutter's Mill at Coloma, in Nisenan country, and the California Gold Rush overran their land. Miners took the rivers, and killings and disease cut the Nisenan to a small remnant within a few years. The Nevada City Rancheria lost its federal recognition in 1964, and its Nisenan people are still working to regain it.
